2. Main points
The following information is for the period from June to August 2026.
Annual growth in employees' average earnings was 3.7% for both regular earnings (excluding bonuses) and total earnings (including bonuses).
Annual growth in real terms, adjusted for inflation using the Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers' housing costs (CPIH), was 0.6% for regular pay and 0.7% for total pay.
Using the Consumer Prices Index excluding owner occupiers' housing costs (CPI) to adjust for inflation, annual growth in real terms was 0.8% for regular pay and 0.9% for total pay.
Annual average regular earnings growth remained at 6.3% for the public sector and 3.0% for the private sector; public sector annual pay growth continues to be affected by variations in the timing of some pay awards this year.
After the public sector, the finances and business sector showed the strongest regular annual growth rate (3.3%).
 !
The estimates in this bulletin come from a survey of businesses. It is not possible to survey every business each month, so these statistics are estimates based on a sample, not precise figures. Average weekly earnings (AWE), for any given month, are the ratio of estimated total pay for the whole economy, divided by the total number of employees. As a result, AWE is not a measure of rates of pay and can be affected by changes in the composition of an enterprise's workforce.

3. Analysis of average weekly earnings
Figure 1: Average weekly earnings for both total and regular pay have shown a steady increase over the long term 
Average weekly earnings in Great Britain, seasonally adjusted, January 2000 to August 2026 
Source: Monthly Wages and Salaries Survey from the Office for National Statistics

Average weekly earnings (AWE) were estimated at £757 for total earnings and £707 for regular earnings in August 2026. Figure 1 shows that AWE have steadily increased over the long term.
Figure 2: Nominal regular earnings saw small increases, over the three previous three-month periods, to 3.7% in June to August 2026
Average weekly earnings annual growth rates in Great Britain, seasonally adjusted, January to March 2001 to June to August 2026
Source: Monthly Wages and Salaries Survey from the Office for National Statistics
 Notes:
Real pay adjusted for inflation using the Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers' housing costs (CPIH).

 Image

The annual growth rate in employees' average regular earnings (excluding bonuses) was 3.7% in June to August 2026 (Figure 2). The annual growth rate has shown a small increase over the three previous three-month periods. 
Annual growth in total earnings (including bonuses) was 3.7% in June to August 2026, down from 3.9% on the previous three-month period. It was last lower than 3.7% in August to October 2020, when it was 2.8%.
In real terms (adjusted for inflation using the Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers' housing costs (CPIH)), annual regular pay growth remained unchanged to the two previous three-month periods at 0.6% in June to August 2026 (Figure 3).
Annual real total pay growth (using CPIH) was 0.7% in June to August 2026, a decrease on the previous three-month period, when it was 1.0%. It was last lower in December 2025 to February 2026, when it was 0.6%.
Figure 3: Real regular earnings growth remained unchanged at 0.6% in June to August 2026 
Real average weekly earnings three-month annual growth rates in Great Britain, seasonally adjusted, and Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers’ housing costs (CPIH) annual rate, January to March 2001 to June to August 2026
Source: Monthly Wages and Salaries Survey, and Consumer price inflation from the Office for National Statistics

 .csv

Figure 3 shows a comparison of three-month average real total pay and regular pay earnings growth rates, and average three-month inflation. CPIH was an average of 3.1% for June to August 2026.
CPIH is our headline measure of inflation. We also publish our supplementary X09: Real average weekly earnings using consumer price inflation (CPI) dataset, excluding owner occupiers' housing costs. Using the Consumer Prices Index (CPI), annual real regular pay growth was 0.8% in June to August 2026. Similarly to real regular pay growth using CPIH, real regular pay growth using CPI has remained steady, showing a similar growth to May to July 2026, following a year and a half of slowing growth.
Annual real total pay growth (using CPI) was 0.9% in June to August 2026, a slight decrease on the previous three-month period, when it was 1.1%. It was last lower than 0.9% in December 2025 to February 2026, when it was 0.8%.
Additional insights into the estimate of growth in median and mean pay are provided in the Earnings and employment from Pay As You Earn Real Time Information, UK bulletin. It also provides a timelier estimate of median pay, but this is subject to revisions. When comparing the comparable measures, the two data sources generally trend well for mean total pay. However, there will be differences between the two data sources because of timing and definitional differences, as described in our Comparison of labour market data sources methodology.
Sector and industry
Figure 4: Regular annual growth was 3.0% for the private sector and 6.3% for the public sector; public sector pay growth continues to be affected by variations in the timings of pay awards this year
Average weekly earnings annual growth rates for total pay (including bonuses) and regular pay (excluding bonuses) by public and private sector in Great Britain, seasonally adjusted, January to March 2001 to June to August 2026 
Source: Monthly Wages and Salaries Survey from the Office for National Statistics
Download this chart Figure 4: Regular annual growth was 3.0% for the private sector and 6.3% for the public sector; public sector pay growth continues to be affected by variations in the timings of pay awards this year
 Image
 .csv
 .xls
Annual average regular earnings growth remained at 6.3% for the public sector in June to August 2026, unchanged on the previous three-month period (Figure 4). The public sector annual pay growth continues to be affected by variations in the timing of some pay awards this year, causing a base effect. For more information go to Public sector pay awards base effect in Section 6. Data sources and quality.
Growth in the private sector has been slowing for several years. However, annual average regular earnings growth increased slightly to 3.0% for the private sector in June to August 2026, compared with 2.9% growth over the three previous three-month periods. 
Annual average total earnings growth was 6.3% for the public sector in June to August 2026. This is a decrease compared with the previous three-month period, when it was 6.6%. This was also affected by the base effect caused by variations in the timing of some pay awards this year.
Annual average total earnings growth was 3.1% for the private sector in June to August 2026. This is a decrease compared with the previous three-month period, when it was 3.3%.
Figure 5: After the public sector, the finance and business services sector showed the strongest annual regular growth rate at 3.3% 
Average weekly earnings annual growth rates for regular pay by sector in Great Britain, seasonally adjusted, June to August 2020 to June to August 2026 
Source: Monthly Wages and Salaries Survey from the Office for National Statistics
Download this chart Figure 5: After the public sector, the finance and business services sector showed the strongest annual regular growth rate at 3.3% 
 Image
 .csv
 .xls
After the public sector, the finance and business services sector showed the strongest regular earnings annual growth rate in June to August 2026, at 3.3% (Figure 5). The construction sector had the slowest regular earnings annual growth rate at 1.1%. The manufacturing sector's regular annual growth rate remained similar to the previous three-month period, at 2.9%. The wholesaling, retailing, hotels and restaurants sector regular annual growth rate decreased from the previous three-month period (3.1%) to 2.7%.
